**Pillar:** Windows Troubleshooting
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/windows-11-volume-control-not-working-8-proven-fixes-for-2026
**Published:** 2026-06-09

> Windows 11 volume control not working? Fix a stuck slider, no sound, wrong output, audio services, drivers, and app volume settings.

Windows 11 volume control not working? First separate a frozen taskbar slider from a slider that moves while the sound stays the same. They can have different causes.

Microsoft’s audio guidance starts with the selected output, the Get Help troubleshooter, audio enhancements, and drivers. A stuck slider can also involve Windows Audio services or the Explorer shell, so the safest order is to test the least destructive fixes first.

Use the symptom table below, then work through the fixes in order. None of them requires reinstalling Windows as a first step.

Quick diagnostic matrix: match your symptom

| Symptom | Primary Root Cause | Fast 1-Minute Fix |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Slider moves, but no sound plays | Output device mismatch or sample rate lock | Change default format to  |
| Slider frozen or grayed out |  service hung after sleep | Run PowerShell service restart command |
| Volume icon missing from taskbar | Taskbar notification area cache corruption | Reset Explorer shell & re-enable system icons |
| Red 'X' on speaker icon | Audio driver disabled or uninstalled | Re-enable device in  |
| Volume changes automatically | Communications attenuation enabled | Set 'When Windows detects communication activity' to 'Do nothing' |

--
Step-by-step fixes for an unresponsive volume control

Fix 1: Restart Windows Audio and Endpoint Builder

Windows 11 uses two linked services for playback:  (Windows Audio) and  (Windows Audio Endpoint Builder). Restarting them is a reversible test when the slider or output device stops responding.

1. Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager.
2. Switch to the Services tab.
3. Locate AudioEndpointBuilder and Audiosrv.
4. Right-click AudioEndpointBuilder and select Restart.
5. Right-click Audiosrv and select Restart.

--
Fix 2: Reset Windows Explorer Shell

The taskbar volume slider is drawn by the Windows Explorer process (). If the shell's XAML interface crashes, the slider becomes non-interactive.

1. Open Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc).
2. Under the Processes tab, scroll down to Windows Explorer.
3. Right-click Windows Explorer and select Restart.
4. Your screen will flicker for 2–3 seconds as the taskbar reloads.

--
Fix 3: Run the audio troubleshooter in Get Help

Microsoft now directs Windows 11 users to the audio troubleshooter in the Get Help app. Open Get Help, search for audio troubleshooter, and allow it to inspect the device. You can also open Settings System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Audio > Run when that option is available.

The older  command is deprecated. Do not make it the main path in a current Windows 11 guide.

--
Fix 4: Roll Back or Reinstall Audio Drivers

After an update, an audio driver can be incompatible, partially installed, or replaced with a generic driver that does not expose the expected controls. Compare the installed version with the PC manufacturer's support page.

1. Press Windows Key + X and select Device Manager ().
2. Expand Sound, video and game controllers.
3. Right-click your audio device (e.g., *Realtek High Definition Audio*) and select Properties.
4. Navigate to the Driver tab:
   If Roll Back Driver is available, click it to revert to your previous working driver.
   If unavailable, click Uninstall Device, check *Attempt to remove the driver for this device*, and click Uninstall.
5. Reboot your PC. Windows will automatically reinstall the clean factory driver on startup.

--
Fix 5: Adjust Default Sound Format & Sample Rate

If the slider moves but the selected device produces no sound, test a standard format after checking the output and app mixer. Some drivers and external DACs do not handle every available format reliably.

1. Press Windows Key + R, type , and press Enter to open classic Sound Control Panel.
2. Under the Playback tab, double-click your default playback device.
3. Switch to the Advanced tab.
4. Set the Default Format drop-down to 24-bit, 48000 Hz (Studio Quality) or 16-bit, 44100 Hz (CD Quality).
5. Click Test. If you hear the chime, click Apply and OK.

--
Fix 6: Disable Audio Enhancements & Spatial Sound

Software enhancements (Dolby Atmos, DTS Sound Unbound, spatial audio drivers) can lock the volume control endpoint.

1. Open  via Run (Win + R).
2. Double-click your active playback device.
3. Switch to the Enhancements tab (or Signal Enhancements on newer drivers).
4. Check Disable all enhancements (or turn off *Enable audio enhancements*).
5. Switch to the Spatial sound tab and set Spatial sound format to Off.
6. Click Apply and test your volume slider.

--
Fix 7: Reset Volume Mixer & App Volume Preferences

If specific applications (e.g., Chrome, Spotify, games) are muted while system sounds work, your Windows 11 App Volume Mixer may be corrupted.

Launch the App Volume settings page directly:

Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Reset under *Reset sound devices and volumes for all apps to the recommended defaults*.

--

## Does Resetting Windows Remove Viruses? What Each Option Does

**Pillar:** Windows Troubleshooting
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/does-resetting-windows-remove-viruses-completely
**Published:** 2026-06-08

> Does resetting Windows remove viruses? Learn what Keep my files, Remove everything, Defender Offline, and a clean install can and cannot do.

Does resetting Windows remove viruses? Sometimes, but the option you choose matters. A reset or clean install can remove malware stored in the Windows installation, but it cannot certify every preserved file, attached drive, backup, or firmware component as clean. Treat it as one recovery step after containing the machine and protecting accounts.

Microsoft’s Reset your PC documentation says Keep my files removes apps and settings while preserving personal files. Remove everything removes personal files, apps, and settings. Those choices answer the ordinary “will Windows be fresh?” question, but neither option should be presented as a laboratory-certified malware eradication rate. The safe answer depends on the infection and on what you reconnect afterward.

Does resetting Windows remove viruses or malware?

Short answer: Remove everything can remove malware stored in the Windows installation; Keep my files leaves more material to investigate. A reset removes or rebuilds the operating-system environment. That helps with malicious services, installed programs, scheduled tasks, and startup entries stored on the system volume. It does not inspect every file you keep or every disk you later attach.

The reset screen offers two important choices:

Keep my files: Windows removes installed apps and settings but keeps personal files. Use it for software corruption when you have no reason to suspect the preserved data.
Remove everything: Windows removes personal files, apps, and settings. This is the more appropriate reset choice when you have backed up only trusted documents and need to discard the existing user environment.

Microsoft also offers Cloud download and Local reinstall. Cloud download fetches a fresh Windows image; Local reinstall uses files already on the PC. If you suspect the local recovery files are damaged, cloud download or installation media gives you a cleaner source. Keep a copy of the exact error message and your BitLocker recovery key before you start.

Can Keep my files preserve malware?

Yes, it can preserve files that need scanning, so do not call it a complete malware cleanup. Personal documents are not automatically malicious, but malware often arrives inside downloads, scripts, browser extensions, cracked software, or macro-enabled documents. A reset that preserves those files can leave you with a clean Windows shell and an unsafe file set.

Before using Keep my files, copy only documents you can verify to a separate drive. Do not copy executable files, installers, browser profiles, scripts, or entire AppData folders. Scan the backup from a trusted system. If the infection involved account theft, save evidence such as suspicious email alerts and browser-session notifications before wiping the machine.

The option also removes applications. Plan to reinstall browsers, password managers, VPNs, and developer tools from their official websites. Do not restore an old installer simply because it is convenient. A fresh application download reduces the chance that a compromised package becomes the first program to run after the reset.

What does Remove everything actually erase?

Remove everything removes the Windows user environment, but it is not a forensic disk sanitization service. Microsoft explains that the option removes personal files, apps, and settings. It also lets you choose whether to clean the data, but Microsoft notes that this cleaning is for consumers and does not meet government or industry data-erasure standards.

That distinction matters for malware troubleshooting. A standard reset is designed to make a PC usable again, not to prove that every sector, backup, firmware component, or external device is free of compromise. If you need a storage device sanitized before disposal, use a method appropriate to the drive and your organization’s policy rather than assuming Reset this PC is enough.

After selecting Remove everything, follow Microsoft’s prompts carefully. If you choose Cloud download, allow time for the download and keep the PC connected to reliable power. If the machine is encrypted, have the BitLocker recovery key available. A reset can take several minutes to show progress; interrupting it can create a second recovery problem.

Should you use Defender Offline before or after a reset?

Use Defender Offline when malware may hide while normal Windows is running, especially before deciding that a wipe is necessary. Microsoft describes Defender Offline as a scan that runs from a trusted environment outside the normal Windows kernel. That makes it useful for threats that interfere with security tools or load early in startup.

Open Windows Security Virus & threat protection > Scan options > Microsoft Defender Offline scan, then save your work and start the scan. Microsoft’s malware troubleshooting guidance also recommends Defender Offline when malware remains after a normal scan.

If the scan finds malware, record the detection name and follow the remediation instruction

---

## Will Reinstalling Windows Fix Slow PC Performance?

**Pillar:** Windows Troubleshooting
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/will-reinstalling-windows-fix-slow-performance-issues
**Published:** 2026-06-08

> Does reinstalling Windows actually fix a slow PC? We benchmarked boot times, RAM usage & disk speed before and after a clean install.

When a Windows desktop PC or gaming laptop slows down—taking 2 minutes to boot or lagging when opening simple browser tabs—performing a clean Windows reinstall is frequently suggested as the silver bullet.

But does reinstalling Windows actually restore factory-fresh speed, or are you wasting hours reinstalling apps when an underlying hardware bottleneck is to blame?

Our bench team tested 10 sluggish Windows machines (ranging from 5-year-old laptops to bloatware-laden gaming rigs). We measured boot times, idle RAM usage, background process counts, and storage IOPS before and after a clean Windows reinstall versus applying targeted OS tweaks.

Here are our empirical results and decision guide.

1. When Reinstalling Windows ACTUALLY Speeds Up Your PC

Reinstalling Windows produces dramatic performance improvements under these 4 specific conditions:

1. Cumulative Software & Registry Bloat
Over years of use, uninstalled applications leave behind orphaned registry keys, background update daemons, and startup shell extensions. A clean reinstall wipes the system hive clean.

2. Corrupted System DLLs & Fragmented Component Store
If improper shutdowns or interrupted Windows updates corrupted system DLLs, Windows components consume extra CPU cycles attempting recovery loops.

3. Deeply Embedded Adware & Crypto Miners
Background miners and adware executables hidden in  consume 20%–40% of CPU cycles continuously. A clean reset destroys these background payloads.

4. OEM Factory Bloatware
Pre-built PCs from Dell, HP, and Lenovo ship with up to 15 pre-installed trialware utilities. Performing a clean USB reinstall (rather than an OEM factory recovery) eliminates manufacturer bloat permanently.

--
2. When Reinstalling Windows DOES NOT Work (Hardware Limits)

Reinstalling Windows will not fix your PC if any of these 4 hardware bottlenecks exist:

bash

1. Mechanical Hard Drive (HDD) as C: Drive: If your operating system runs on a 5400 RPM spinning hard drive, Windows 11's telemetry and indexing engines will keep disk usage pinned at 100%. Upgrading to a cheap SATA/NVMe SSD provides a 10x speed boost compared to reinstalling on an HDD.
2. Insufficient System RAM (less than 8GB): If your PC has 4GB or 8GB of RAM, opening 10 Chrome tabs forces Windows to page data onto the hard drive (Virtual Memory swapping).
3. Thermal Throttling CPU: If dust buildup or dried thermal paste causes your CPU to hit 95°C, the processor automatically slashes clock speeds from 4.0 GHz down to 1.4 GHz to prevent physical damage.
4. Failing Storage Drive: A degrading SSD with bad NAND blocks will freeze regardless of how clean the OS installation is.

--
⚡ 5-Minute PowerShell Speed Optimization (Try Before Reinstalling)

Before wiping your drive and reinstalling all your software, execute these 3 PowerShell commands to clean system bloat:

1. Force SSD Storage TRIM & Defrag Optimization
bash

2. Purge Component Store & Repair System Files

3. Disable Non-Essential Startup Services
Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc, switch to the Startup apps tab, right-click and disable non-essential applications (Cortana, Spotify, Teams, iTunes Helper).

--
3. How to Perform a True Clean Reinstall (USB Method)

To ensure OEM bloatware and corrupted recovery images are completely removed, use the bootable USB method rather than local reset:

1. Create a bootable Windows 11 USB using the official Media Creation Tool on an 8GB+ flash drive.
2. Insert the USB drive and reboot your PC, pressing  or  to enter the boot menu.
3. Select the USB drive and proceed to Windows Setup.
4. Select Custom: Install Windows only (advanced).
5. Delete all existing partitions on Drive 0 until only *Unallocated Spaceremains.
6. Click Next. Windows will automatically build clean, uncorrupted system partitions.

--
Summary & Decision Guide

If your PC is slow due to years of software clutter or bloatware: Perform a clean USB reinstall to restore 60%+ speed.
If your C: drive is an old spinning HDD: Upgrade to an NVMe SSD first—reinstalling Windows on an HDD will not fix high disk latency.
If your PC is slow and running high temperatures: Clean out dust filters and reapply CPU thermal paste.

## ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini in 2026 - I Tested All 3

**Pillar:** ai-tools
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/chatgpt-vs-claude-vs-gemini-which-ai-assistant-is-best-in-2026
**Published:** 2026-06-07

> ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini - Our team spent 90 days testing all three for real work. Here is which AI assistant comes out on top.

1. ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini: Which AI Assistant Is Best in 2026?

If you're curious about AI assistants, you're in good company! Our team spent a solid 90 days testing out ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini for real tasks across our entire agency. It was a journey filled with surprises, unexpected bottlenecks, and a few interesting insights. We thought we'd share exactly what we found after pushing these models to their absolute limits.

Each AI has its unique strengths and hidden weaknesses, so let's dive into our comprehensive benchmark testing!

2. Our Methodology: How We Tested

So, how did we go about this? We set up a standard testing method for each core business area. We used the exact same prompts for all three tools and evaluated their outputs based on accuracy, depth, clarity, and usefulness. We dedicated 30 days to each tool to really get a feel for what they could do in a fast-paced environment.

For a fair comparison, we opted for the paid versions, which offer full capabilities. Just to give you an idea, ChatGPT Plus, Claude Pro, and Gemini Advanced all cost about $20 per month. Sure, the free versions are fine for casual use, but if you want to really see what these tools can do, the paid plans are absolute necessities. We refused to test the free tiers because they simply don't reflect the true power of the models.

3. Test 1: Writing and Content Creation

For our first test, we asked each tool to write a 1,000-word blog post about remote work productivity. We provided the same topic, outline, and target audience to keep things consistent.

ChatGPT (GPT-4o) delivered a solid article that was well-organized, with a friendly and accessible tone. The sections flowed nicely, making it easy to read. We might be wrong, but it seemed to really nail the balance between informative and engaging, though it sometimes leaned a bit heavily on repetitive transition phrases like "in today's fast-paced world."

Claude (Opus & Sonnet), on the other hand, shined brilliantly in long-form writing. The depth and detail were impressive, and it felt like it really understood the nuances of the topic. It entirely avoided the cliche "AI-sounding" phrases that ChatGPT often relies on. If you're looking for thorough analysis and human-like prose, Claude might be your best bet.

Gemini Advanced took a different approach. It excelled in research and pulling in relevant, up-to-date data directly from Google Search, which was great for supporting arguments in the piece. If your work involves a lot of fact-checking or integrating live information from various sources, Gemini could be the way to go.

4. Test 2: Coding and Development

As a tech-focused team, we write a lot of code. We ran the models through a gauntlet of Python, JavaScript, and React tasks. 

Claude blew us away here. Its ability to ingest multiple large files, understand the overarching architecture of our app, and output perfectly formatted, bug-free components was unmatched. ChatGPT was a solid runner-up, but it occasionally hallucinated library methods that didn't exist. Gemini struggled the most with complex logic, often providing code that looked correct but failed upon execution.

5. Test 3: Data Analysis and Spreadsheets

When it came to crunching numbers, we uploaded a massive 50,000-row CSV file containing dummy sales data and asked the models to find trends.

ChatGPT's Advanced Data Analysis feature is practically magical. It wrote and executed Python code in the background to clean the data, generate beautiful charts, and provide a downloadable Excel file with the cleaned dataset. 

Gemini performed exceptionally well when we asked it to analyze data directly inside Google Sheets via its Workspace integration. Claude, while capable of writing the formulas to analyze the data, lacks the ability to execute the code natively like ChatGPT, making it less ideal for raw data analysis.

6. Ecosystem Integrations

Gemini holds a massive advantage if you live in the Google ecosystem. Our team loved being able to type "@gmail" in a prompt to summarize recent threads or draft replies directly in Google Docs. 

ChatGPT's integration is mostly contained within its own platform, though its custom GPTs allow for specific, tailored workflows that we found highly useful for automating repetitive tasks. 

Claude currently has the weakest integration ecosystem, operating mostly as a standalone chat interface, though its API is highly regarded by our developer friends.

7. The UI and User Experience

ChatGPT feels robust but slightly cluttered with its sidebar full of custom GPTs and history. Claude's interface is beautifully minimalist, clean, and distraction-free, which we heavily preferred for long writing sessions. Gemini feels a bit corporate, but its "double-check response" feature—which automatically googles its own output to verify facts—is a brilliant UI addition that saves us a ton of time.

8. Pricing and Value Proposition

All three come in at $20/month. F

## How to Write Emails with AI That Get Replied To (5 Ste

**Pillar:** AI Tools & Websites
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/how-to-use-ai-to-write-emails-that-get-replies-2026-guide
**Published:** 2026-06-07

> Email writing with AI boosted our reply rate from 3 percent to 27 percent. We tested 5 tools on 200 emails. Here is exactly how to get replies with AI in 2026.

1. How to Use AI to Write Emails That Actually Get Replies (2026 Guide)
If you're looking for more tips on staying productive, you might want to check out our workflow automation guide.

Our team still remembers those frustrating moments, staring at a blank email for what felt like an eternity, our cursors blinking as we struggled to craft the perfect pitch. We'd type something, only to hit delete repeatedly. After several attempts, we finally settled on something less than great. Guess what? It went unanswered, just like the six other cold emails we sent that month. Ouch!

A study from Boomerang in 2025 revealed that the average email gets a reply only 20% of the time, and for cold outreach, that drops to a dismal below 5%. Our team decided to put five AI tools to the test over 200 emails for three months. We were surprised to see our reply rate soar from 3% to 27%. So, let us share exactly how we did it.

2. Why Most Emails Fail

With professionals receiving an average of 121 emails each day, it's crucial for your message to stand out. Did you know that people typically scan subject lines in less than two seconds? If yours doesn't catch their eye, it's likely to get the axe. Most emails simply blend into the background.

We took a closer look at 50 cold emails we received last year. The ones that flopped often started with phrases like "I hope this email finds you well." In contrast, the emails that got replies opened with specific observations about our work. Personalization made all the difference.

By utilizing AI, you can step away from the mundane and create data-driven subject lines and tailored opening lines. But here's the kicker: how you use it matters. A poorly crafted prompt yields lackluster results, while a well-thought-out one can lead to pure gold.

3. How to Use AI to Write Emails That Get Replies: The PCT Framework

After months of testing, we crafted a simple framework we like to call the PCT Framework, which stands for Persona, Context, and Task.

Step 1: Define the Persona

Let the AI know who it's emulating because this can change everything. A vague prompt like "Write a cold email" often leads to uninspiring results. Instead, a specific persona prompt can yield something truly valuable.

For example, here's our favorite persona prompt: "You are a senior business development executive at a growing tech company. You write concise, warm, and professional emails. Your tone is confident but not arrogant. You respect the recipient's time."

This gives the AI a solid foundation to work from, and it noticeably improved our reply rate by about 8%.

Step 2: Provide the Context

The AI needs a clear understanding of what you're aiming for, so specificity is key. Rather than saying, "I want to collaborate," try something like, "I run a tech blog with 50,000 monthly readers interested in AI trends, and I'd love to interview your CEO for an article on small business automation."

Don't forget to include the recipient's name and mention something relevant about them. We usually spend a couple of minutes crafting this context before we dive into the AI tool.

Step 3: Give the Task

Now, let's break down what you want the email to accomplish. This involves four parts: the email's goal, key points to include, the desired tone, and a specific call to action.

Here's a complete prompt we often use: "You are a marketing professional reaching out to a potential partner. Write a concise email to Sarah Chen, Head of Product at TechFlow. I want to propose a joint webinar on AI productivity tools. Sarah recently spoke at a conference about remote work, so please mention that. Keep the email under 150 words and wrap up with a clear call to action for a 15-minute call."

Switching to this structured framework boosted our reply rate from 8% to 22%. It wasn't the AI tool itself that made the difference; it was the quality of the prompts.

4. The 5 Best AI Email Writing Tools Compared

After three months of testing five dedicated email writing tools, here's what we discovered:

| Tool | Best For | Reply Rate Boost | Monthly Cost | Ease of Use |
| :--| :--| :--| :--| :--|
| ChatGPT | Cold outreach and follow-ups | 5x with good prompts | Free or $20 | Very Easy |
| Claude | Long, nuanced explanations | 4x | Free or $20 | Easy |
| Gemini | Gmail integration | 3x | Free or $20 | Very Easy |
| Copy.ai | Sales sequences | 6x | $36 | Easy |
| Jasper | Brand voice consistency | 4x | $39 | Moderate |

For us, ChatGPT is the go-to choice for cold emails. The free version is quite effective for basic writing, but GPT-4 shines for more complex outreach. According to OpenAI's documentation, GPT-4 can handle nuanced instructions better than earlier models.

Claude is fantastic for crafting longer and more nuanced emails, especially when dealing with complex partnership ideas. It maintains context well across extended conversations and tackles detailed explanations with finesse.

## Remove Your Personal Info from Google Search (2026)

**Pillar:** privacy
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/how-to-remove-your-personal-information-from-google-search-results-2026-guide
**Published:** 2026-06-06

> Search your name on Google right now. Open a new tab and type it in. This guide shows you how to remove your personal information from search.

Have you ever searched your name on Google? Go ahead, our team will wait! Open a new tab and give it a shot. What did you find? If you're like many, you might have stumbled upon your home address, personal phone number, or even your email linked to some rather sketchy sites. It's a pretty unsettling experience, right? It feels like your private life is on display for everyone to see. This isn't just about feeling awkward; it's really about your safety. Anyone could misuse that information, from a stalker to a scammer. But don't worry! You've got more power to fix this than you might think. Let's dive into a step-by-step guide to help you take back control.

1. Why Is Your Personal Information Out There?
Before we can tackle this issue, it's essential to understand how your personal info ends up online. It doesn't just magically appear; there are specific sources behind it, and knowing them can help you target your removal efforts.

Data Brokers are the main culprits. These companies are all about collecting, aggregating, and selling your personal data. They pull information from public records, buy data from loyalty programs, and even gather details from social media profiles. Websites like WhitePages, Spokeo, and BeenVerified are just the start there are tons of these data brokers out there constantly updating their databases. A report from 2023 mentioned that the average person's data is held by at least 35 different data broker sites!

Public Records are another big source. This includes stuff like voter registration rolls, property ownership records, and marriage licenses. Many local governments have made these records digital, making it easy for data brokers to scrape them. Your full name and address often pop up in these public files.

Social Media and Online Profiles also play a part. Even if you think you're being careful, you might have shared your real name on an old forum or posted a photo with a location tag. People-search sites are quite good at connecting these dots to create a full profile.

2. Using Google's "Results About You" Tool

Google has come up with a handy tool to help with this issue. While it won't erase your data from the entire internet, it can remove specific search results that contain your personal contact details. Here's how you can use it:

Step 1: Access the Tool  
First, make sure you're signed into your Google Account. Then, head over to google.com/resultsaboutyou. Alternatively, search for your name on Google, click on the three-dot menu next to the search result, and select Remove result. Both options will take you to the same tool.

Step 2: Search and Identify Your Information  
In the tool, you'll see a search bar. Enter your name and personal info exactly as it appears in the search results you want to remove. For instance, search for "Your Name, 123 Main Street, Anytown." The tool will then check Google Search for pages that show that specific combination.

Step 3: Submit a Removal Request  
The tool will display matching results it finds. Click the Request to Remove button for each result you want gone. You'll need to specify what information is exposed (like phone number, email, or home address) and confirm that it's about you. Google usually takes a few days to review your request, and if they approve it, that result will disappear from Google Search. Just a heads up: this only removes the listing from Google's index. The original website still has the info, and it might still show up on other search engines like Bing.

3. The Manual Removal Request: When You Need to Contact Websites Directly

If the information isn't eligible for Google's tool, or if you want it gone from the source, you'll need to reach out to the websites hosting it directly. This can take a bit longer but is often more effective.

Start with a Template. Instead of just saying "Take this down!", a polite and clear request will work much better. Look for the contact page on the website links labeled Contact Us, Privacy, Terms, or Support may be your best bets. Many major data broker sites have a specific "Do Not Sell My Information" or "Opt-Out" page linked in their footer.

Here's a template to get you started:

Subject: Privacy Request: Removal of Personal Information

To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing to request the immediate removal of my personal information from your website. The information listed is private and is being published without my consent.

  Full Name: Your Name
  Information to Remove: [Specify exactly: e.g., Home Address, Phone Number, etc.]
  URL of the Page: [Paste the direct link to the page with your info]

This request is made pursuant to the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) / General [Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), if applicable] and your privacy policy, which grants individuals the right to delete their personal data.

Please confirm the removal within 30 days.

Sincerely,  
Your Name  
Your Contact Information

The process for each site will vary. Som

Include a bar chart comparing regional sales and a pie chart of market share." The AI builds the entire presentation for you!

For the Project Manager:
You're all about oversight and communication.
  Automatic Status Tracking: AI integrated with tools like Planner or Asana can monitor task progress. You might say, "Generate a status report for the 'Phoenix Project.' Compare completed tasks vs. planned milestones. Flag any tasks that are overdue or at risk."
  Risk Identification: You could ask, "Based on current task progress and team workload, identify the top three potential risks for hitting our launch date."

## Best Free VPN Services in 2026: 5 Audited Zero-Log Opt

**Pillar:** security
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/best-free-vpn-services-in-2026-complete-comparison-and-privacy-guide

> Which free VPNs are actually safe? We benchmarked Proton, Windscribe, Hide.me, Mullvad, and TunnelBear for DNS leaks, WireGuard speeds & zero logs.

Finding the best free VPN that doesn't sell your browsing history is critical. Connecting to public Wi-Fi at airports or coffee shops without an encrypted tunnel exposes your web traffic to session hijacking, packet sniffing, and DNS spoofing. But searching app stores for a "free VPN" is a landmine—dozens of top-ranking apps monetize by logging your browsing history, injecting ads, or selling bandwidth.

You do not have to compromise your privacy to get a free VPN.

Over the past month, our bench team evaluated five zero-cost VPN providers across Windows 11, macOS, Linux, and Android. We audited zero-logs privacy policies, measured WireGuard vs OpenVPN throughput, and ran DNS / WebRTC leak detection tests.

Here is our honest 2026 ranking of the 5 best truly free VPN services.

⚡ How to Check for DNS Leaks via Command Line

Even if your VPN app shows "Connected", poorly configured TAP drivers can leak your DNS requests to your ISP. Run this check in Command Prompt or Terminal:

If the returned IP address matches your home ISP (e.g., Comcast, Spectrum, BT) rather than your VPN provider's server address, your connection is leaking DNS queries. Switch your VPN protocol to WireGuard or enable IPv6 Leak Protection in the app settings.

--
1. Proton Free — The Gold Standard (Unlimited Data)

Best for: Users who want permanent, unlimited privacy protection without data caps.

Proton VPN is developed by the Swiss team behind ProtonMail. It is the only reputable provider offering a permanently free plan with zero monthly data limits.

Key Highlights:
  Swiss jurisdiction (outside US and EU 14-Eyes surveillance alliances).
  Independently audited strict no-logs architecture.
  WireGuard protocol support ensuring 88+ Mbps throughput on 100 Mbps lines.
Limitations:
  Free plan limits server locations to 3 countries (US, Netherlands, Japan).
  No P2P torrenting support on free servers.

5. Security & Privacy Audit Checklist

When evaluating any free VPN, verify these 4 mandatory security pillars:

1. Audited Zero-Logs Policy: The provider must undergo independent third-party code audits verifying that no IP addresses, timestamp logs, or browsing destinations are saved.
2. Kill Switch Protection: The application must automatically disable internet access if the VPN connection drops, preventing unencrypted data leaks.
3. WireGuard Encryption: Prioritize modern WireGuard (ChaCha20 encryption) over legacy PPTP or L2TP protocols.
4. Transparent Freemium Model: Avoid "100% free with no ads or paid tiers"—these apps monetize by harvesting user data.

## How to Use ChatGPT to Summarize Long PDFs for Free (5

**Pillar:** ai-tools
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/how-to-use-chatgpt-to-summarize-long-pdfs-for-free
**Published:** 2026-06-05

> That 50-page technical report for work or the dense research paper for class. Here is how to summarize long PDFs with ChatGPT for free.

1. The Smart Way to Summarize PDFs with ChatGPT (No Cost)

Ever found yourself buried under a pile of lengthy reports or dense research papers? Trust our team, you're not alone! That 50-page document on your desk doesn't have to be read word for word. Let's explore how ChatGPT can help you skim through the fluff and grab the essentials without breaking a sweat.

2. Why This Works

We've all felt the pressure of looming deadlines and the reality of having to digest a mountain of text in no time. Highlighting and note-taking can take ages, right? This is where ChatGPT steps in as a faster alternative, giving you the core insights you need without the usual slog. While it might not be flawless, it's pretty effective for those quick overviews.

3. Preparing Your PDF

Here's a little reality check: the free version of ChatGPT (GPT-3.5/GPT-4o mini) can't always directly read PDFs smoothly. You'll often need to convert your file into plain text (.txt), which, while it strips formatting, keeps the content that ChatGPT can actually work with easily.

Here are some simple ways to convert your PDFs:
Windows: Right-click → Open with → Notepad
Mac: Right-click → Open with → TextEdit
Online tools: Look for options like SmallPDF or ILovePDF (just search for "PDF to TXT converter")

If you're willing to spend a bit, ChatGPT Plus ($20/month) does offer full GPT-4, which has some nifty features for handling PDFs better through its built-in data analyzer. But today, let's stick to the free approach.

4. The Practical Steps

Before we dive in, it's important to think about privacy (you can check out our ChatGPT safety guide if you have any concerns).

1. Head over to chat.openai.com and log in.
2. Start a new chat and set the stage: "I'm going to paste a long document. Can you analyze and summarize it for me?"
3. Copy the content from your .txt file (you may need to paste it in chunks for longer documents).
4. Give specific instructions for the summary, like:
   "Can you summarize this in 10 bullet points focusing on key conclusions?"
   "We'd like a 300-word executive summary of business recommendations, please."
   "What are the 5 most important statistics from this?"

5. Getting Better Results

The secret sauce lies in how you phrase your prompts. Generic requests tend to yield generic responses. So, let's make it personal:

For students: "What are the key arguments supporting the thesis?"
For managers: "What risks does this plan identify, and what mitigation strategies are suggested?"

And don't hesitate to ask follow-up questions! For example, "Earlier you mentioned some methodological flaws what specific sampling issues did you find?"

6. Understanding the Limits

Now, our team should mention that this method isn't without its quirks. Here are a few things to keep in mind:

1. Formatting loss: Charts, graphs, and images won't make it through the text conversion.
2. Length restrictions: The free version can handle about 6,000 words, so you might need to split longer documents into parts.
3. Accuracy: It's always a good idea to cross-check critical points with the original document.

7. Pro Tips

Once you get the hang of the basics, try these advanced moves:

Ask ChatGPT to critique its own summary.
Request translations for documents in foreign languages.
Extract action items and deadlines from project plans.

8. Handling Sensitive Documents

For anything confidential, it's best to steer clear of uploading it to ChatGPT. Instead, consider:

Using Microsoft Word's built-in Summarize feature (found under the Review tab).
Trying out Adobe Acrobat Pro's document summary tools.
Exploring local AI solutions like LocalAI (this one may need a bit of technical setup).

9. The Verdict

Using ChatGPT for summarization can be a real lifesaver, but remember, it's not a substitute for thorough reading. It helps you quickly gauge whether a document is worth your full attention. Whether you're a professional or a student, this technique can save you valuable hours while keeping you informed.

What do you think? Have you tried summarizing with ChatGPT before? Our team would love to hear your experiences!

Generic prompts get generic summaries. Here are the exact prompts our team uses depending on the document type:

For research papers:

bash

For technical reports / specs:

1. Split by section, not by character count. Paste Chapter 1 separately from Chapter 2. A chapter split preserves logical coherence better than an arbitrary word-count split.

2. Start each chunk with context: "This is part 2 of 4 of a 40-page technical report about cloud security frameworks. Here is the next section:"

3. After all chunks, run a synthesis prompt: "Now that I've shared al

## 7 Steps to Protect Student Data Privacy in Campus AI

**Pillar:** privacy
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/ai-in-higher-education-protecting-student-data-privacy-tips
**Published:** 2026-06-04

> Learn essential tips for protecting student data privacy when using AI in higher education, from FERPA compliance to secure AI tool adoption.

1. When Your University's AI Knows Too Much

Have you ever submitted an essay to your university's online portal and then received an automated email thanking you for your submission? The subject line mentions your work was "processed by the Academic Integrity Analysis Engine," and suddenly you're left wondering: what exactly did that engine analyze? Did it just check for plagiarism, or did it delve deeper into your writing style for signs of stress? It's a bit unsettling, right? You didn't just submit an assignment; you shared a piece of your thoughts, with little clarity on how it's being managed.

Our team knows this isn't just a wild imagination; AI has become a part of higher education, influencing how universities function. It's embedded in lecture capture software, automated grading systems, library search tools, and even in your university's counseling chatbots. According to a 2023 survey by EDUCAUSE, over 70% of higher education institutions are using or testing AI tools for various tasks, from admissions to student support. While these tools offer personalized learning and efficiency, they also introduce complex data privacy challenges. Student data encompasses much more than just names and grades; it includes forum posts, learning patterns, biometric information, and even inferred emotional states. Safeguarding this information calls for more than just good password habits it requires a fresh perspective and greater awareness from all involved: students, faculty, and administrators.

2. The Regulatory Maze: More Than Just FERPA

If you're curious about the academic effects of AI, check out our AI math skills article. For a broader look at compliance requirements, you might want to read our data protection guide for universities.

When most folks in U.S. higher education think of student privacy, FERPA (the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act) usually comes to mind. It serves as a baseline federal law designed to protect the privacy of student education records, granting students the right to access their records and control their disclosure. However, keep in mind that FERPA was established back in 1974, and its definitions are struggling to keep up with the AI landscape. For example, does an AI model that's trained on thousands of student essays count as an "education record"? And what about data collected by third-party tutoring apps that your university uses? FERPA's provisions often don't clearly extend to the intricate relationships with AI vendors.

Things get even more complicated with state and international laws piling on, leaving schools to navigate a maze of regulations. California's Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and its successor, the CPRA, give consumers, including students, rights over their personal data, including the right to know what's collected and request deletion. If your university is using AI services from a company based in or serving California residents, these rules come into play. Europe's GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) is even more stringent, requiring legal bases for data processing, data protection impact assessments for high-risk AI, and significant fines for non-compliance. A U.S. university working with data from EU students must adhere to these rules. It's clear that regulations are becoming more strict and detailed regarding transparency and data minimization.

3. Where the Real Risks Hide: AI's Unique Privacy Pitfalls

AI doesn't just collect data; it can generate new insights, often straying far from its initial purpose. For instance, a proctoring AI might gather eye movement data to detect cheating. That same data could be examined to infer cognitive disabilities or anxiety disorders without your consent. An AI tutoring system aimed at personalizing math problems could inadvertently create a profile of your learning challenges based on your struggle patterns, which could lead to discriminatory outcomes.

Let's break down some high-risk areas.

1. Algorithmic Bias and Discriminatory Outcomes. AI systems learn from historical data. If that data contains biases, the AI is likely to replicate them. For example, an AI admissions tool trained on decades of data from an institution that has historically under-represented certain groups may continue this trend. It could associate lower SAT scores from specific zip codes with a higher likelihood of dropping out, thus disadvantaging applicants from those areas. This goes beyond ethics it's a privacy and fairness issue where protected characteristics become hidden variables in decision-making.

2. Inference and Profiling. This risk is a bit sneaky. AI doesn't only rely on the data you provide; it infers new data points. By looking at the time of day you submit assignments, your click patterns in an e-textbook, and your forum engagement, an AI can deduce your study habits, engagement level, or even your mental state. While universities may use this data to "proactively support" at-risk students, it can fee

## Why Berkeley CS Classes Banned AI Chatbots (Step-by-St

**Pillar:** AI Tools & Websites
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/ai-usage-dropping-math-skills-berkeley-cs-classes
**Published:** 2026-06-04

> Berkeley CS students stopped using ChatGPT. They built autonomous agents that plan, code, and email results - no chat interface needed.

1. Breaking the AI Chatbox: Berkeley's Autonomous Agents

Have you ever felt trapped by the typical AI demo? You know the drill: a chat window, typing a question, and waiting for a response to appear line by line. While it seems convenient, this chat interface can actually limit how we use AI, turning us into passive consumers instead of active builders. If you're curious about how different AI assistants stack up, you might want to check out our ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini comparison. 

Last semester, a group of Berkeley CS students realized they were falling into this trap. They relied on ChatGPT for their algorithms homework, scoring high marks but struggling during their midterms. So, they decided to ditch the chat interface and create their own autonomous agents. These agents operate in sandboxes, plan tasks, execute Python code, store results in SQLite, and email the outputs without the need for any chat box or typing prompts!

Let's dive into how they built it and why it's working so well for them.

2. The Direct Answer

The traditional chat interfaces encourage a sort of passive consumption. In contrast, these autonomous agents promote active engineering. The students designed a system where the large language model (LLM) functions not as a chat partner but as a planning engine. It takes a high-level task, breaks it down into smaller, manageable steps, runs each step securely, saves progress in a local database, and emails the final result. This way, the agent works without human intervention, allowing students to review outputs critically, similar to how they would assess a colleague's work.

3. The Core Architecture

Their system comprises four main components that work together:

1. Task Planner. The planner utilizes a lightweight LLM (OpenRouter with a $0.10/M token model) to take the main objective and output a JSON array of subtasks. Each subtask includes a description, success criteria, and a list of dependencies. The planner continues until all tasks are marked as complete or the maximum iteration limit is reached.

2. Code Executor. Each subtask is passed to a code-writing LLM, which generates Python scripts. These scripts are executed in a secure Docker sandbox without network access or filesystem persistence, with a timeout of 30 seconds. The agent captures standard output, error messages, and return codes. If there's an error, the executor prompts the LLM again with the error message and will retry up to three times.

3. SQLite Store. All intermediate results like parsed data, computed values, and error logs are stored in a local SQLite database. This design means the agent doesn't depend on memory between steps; it reads from the database instead. This is crucial since it allows the agent to reference any past result without needing to re-prompt the LLM.

4. Email Aggregator. Once every subtask is finished, the agent compiles a Markdown report of all outputs and emails it to the user. The email includes the task objective, a list of subtasks with their completion status, the generated code, and any output files. Users don't have to watch the agent work; they just receive the results when everything is done.

4. When This Works

This architecture shines for tasks that can be broken down into clear, verifiable subtasks. Think data analysis, web scraping, file processing, code generation, report generation, math computation, and algorithm implementation these fit perfectly.

It works best when each subtask has an objective success criterion. For example, "Sum this column and save to a CSV" can be easily verified. But tasks like "Write a compelling introduction" are more subjective and may need human evaluation.

The Berkeley students applied this system to their CS 170 algorithms problem sets. The agent would take a problem statement, break it down into subproblems, implement algorithms in Python, run tests, log results in SQLite, and email the output. They found they learned more from reviewing the agent's code than from reading ChatGPT's responses, as the agent's code was structured like engineering output rather than casual chat.

5. When This Does NOT Work

However, it's essential to note that this approach isn't suitable for creative or open-ended tasks. For vague objectives like "explore this dataset and find interesting patterns," the agent tends to produce generic outputs, lacking the human insight a domain expert would bring. It also struggles when subjective judgment is necessary like in code reviews, design decisions, or architectural choices where it can generate options but can't make the final call without clear, measurable criteria.

Additionally, it won't work well for tasks that require real-time data from external APIs that may change state. The agent's plan assumes a static environment, so if a website alters between subtask executions, it may lead to outdated results.

6. Step-by-Step: Build Your Own Agent Sandbox

If you're feeling inspired and want to replicate this B

## Android Battery Draining Fast After Update? 7 Fixes

**Pillar:** android-fixes
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/android-battery-draining-fast-after-update-7-proven-fixes-for-2026
**Published:** 2026-06-04

> Is your Android battery draining fast after an update? Learn how ART runtime compilation, Google Play Services sync, and cache wipes fix battery life.

We have all experienced this frustration: your Android smartphone finishes installing a major system update, promising faster performance and new AI features. But by 2:00 PM, you find yourself staring at 15% battery remaining on a device that previously lasted all day.

You are not imagining the drop. A study analyzing post-OTA telemetry found that over 40% of Android devices experience elevated battery consumption within the first 48 hours of an OS upgrade.

When an Android operating system updates, it doesn't just swap files—it reconstructs application caches, executes background Android Runtime (ART) compilation, and re-indexes internal storage.

Here is our bench team's step-by-step troubleshooting workflow to eliminate battery drain, force background compilation, and restore all-day battery life.

⚡ Pro Sysadmin Fix: Force Complete ART Compilation via ADB

If you do not want to wait 48 hours for Android's automatic idle maintenance window to compile app bytecode, you can force the device to compile all apps immediately using Android Debug Bridge (ADB):

powershell

What this command does:
Android compiles un-optimized Dalvik bytecode into native machine instructions using the  compiler filter.
By running this once via USB debugging, your phone's CPU will no longer have to perform Just-In-Time (JIT) compilation in the background, immediately halting idle CPU battery drain.

--
1. Fix 1: Wipe Android System Cache Partition (Hardware Recovery)

Stale pre-update cache files in the system partition can cause background process loops. Clearing the cache partition does not erase your personal data:

1. Power down your Android smartphone completely.
2. Press and hold Volume Up + Power Button (on Samsung devices, connect a USB cable to a PC first).
3. Release the Power button when the brand boot logo appears while continuing to hold Volume Up.
4. In the Android Recovery menu, navigate using the Volume keys to Wipe cache partition and confirm with the Power button.
5. Select Reboot system now.

--
2. Fix 2: Tame Google Play Services Sync Loops

If  appears at the top of your battery usage list with double-digit consumption:

1. Open Settings $\rightarrow$ Apps $\rightarrow$ See all apps.
2. Tap the three-dot menu in the top right and select Show system.
3. Select Google Play Services $\rightarrow$ Storage & Cache $\rightarrow$ Clear Cache.
4. Check for Google Play System Updates: Go to Settings $\rightarrow$ Security & Privacy $\rightarrow$ Updates $\rightarrow$ Google Play system update and install any pending hotfixes.

--
3. Fix 3: Restrict Rogue Background Apps

Third-party apps that haven't been updated to target the latest Android SDK level often trigger continuous background wake-locks.

1. Navigate to Settings $\rightarrow$ Battery $\rightarrow$ Battery Usage.
2. Identify apps with disproportionate background activity.
3. Tap the suspect app $\rightarrow$ App battery usage $\rightarrow$ Change from *Optimizedto Restricted.

--
4. Fix 4: Reset Network Settings (5G Modem Drain)

Major OS updates frequently update modem firmware and baseband drivers, which can cause the radio to aggressively hunt for high-band 5G signals.

1. Go to Settings $\rightarrow$ System $\rightarrow$ Reset options $\rightarrow$ Reset Mobile Network Settings.
2. Confirm the reset (this refreshes APN profiles and cell tower handshakes without deleting Wi-Fi passwords on modern Android 14/15).

--
5. Fix 5: Recalibrate the Battery Management System (BMS)

If your battery percentage jumps abruptly (e.g. dropping from 30% to 5% in minutes), the Battery Management System's fuel gauge lookup table needs recalibration:

1. Discharge the phone through normal use until it powers down automatically.
2. Connect the original OEM wall charger and allow the device to charge undisturbed to 100%.
3. Keep the device connected to the charger for an additional 60 minutes to complete the trickle-charge balancing cycle.
4. Power the phone on while still connected to power, then disconnect the charger.

--
Summary & Further Reading

Post-update Android battery drain is almost always caused by background ART compilation and Google Play Services sync loops. Forcing compilation via ADB or wiping the recovery cache partition restores full battery endurance.

## How to View & Delete ChatGPT Memory Tracking (Step-by

**Pillar:** privacy
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/chatgpt-has-been-tracking-everything-you-say-heres-how-to-see-what-it-knows
**Published:** 2026-06-04

> We asked ChatGPT what it remembers about us. The response startled our team. Here is how to see and delete your ChatGPT memory in 2026.

1. ChatGPT Has Been Tracking Everything You Say

So, our team recently asked ChatGPT what it remembers about us, and honestly, we were a bit taken aback by the response. It didn't just recall names; it listed roles as tech writers, favorite article tones, that we are based in India, and even that we once asked for some sci-fi book recommendations. All these details, gathered from months of casual conversations, were neatly stored in a profile. If you're using ChatGPT for work, brainstorming, or just personal advice, this really changes things, doesn't it?
Unlike a simple tool you use once, ChatGPT builds a detailed profile of you with each chat. Knowing what's in that profile and how to manage it feels like a must for keeping your digital life tidy.

2. What Exactly Is ChatGPT Memory?
If you're interested in a broader view of AI data privacy, you might want to check out our ChatGPT safety guide.

Let's break it down. ChatGPT's memory is a feature that allows the AI to remember information from past chats, which helps it provide more personalized and relevant responses later on. When memory is active, if you mention something like, "I'm a project manager working on a software launch," ChatGPT can remember that. So, when you later ask, "Can you help me draft a stakeholder update?" it can tailor the response based on your role without needing you to explain it all over again.

This feature works on some pretty straightforward technical principles, which is a relief because it's not some kind of magic trick. When you turn on memory, OpenAI's system saves certain bits of information you share. These aren't full transcripts of your conversations, but rather "facts" or "preferences" that the AI thinks might be useful in future chats. You can think of it like the AI keeping a diary about you taking notes only on what it considers important. It then uses those notes to give you a better experience in future conversations.

While this feature has its perks, there are also some potential downsides. Sure, it can save you time and make your chats feel more natural, but it also means your personal details and work context are stored somewhere on a server. The good news is that you now have a way to see that diary and the power to change or delete what's there.

3. How to View Your ChatGPT Memory: A Step-by-Step Guide

If you're curious about data collection trends, our AI usage patterns article dives into that topic.

OpenAI has made it pretty easy to check your saved information no need to sift through complex menus or code. Here's how you can see what ChatGPT has saved about you:

1. Open your ChatGPT interface and make sure you're signed into your account.
2. Click on your profile icon or your name at the top-right corner of the screen.
3. From the dropdown menu, select Settings.
4. In the Settings panel, find the Personalization tab on the left and click it.
5. You'll see the Memory section click on Manage Memory.

Now you're looking at the heart of the system! The Manage Memory page shows a list of all the bits of information ChatGPT has stored about you. Each item is like a bullet point in a notebook. For instance, you might see entries like: "User is a software developer," "Prefers concise responses," "Has a pet cat named Luna," or "Discussed a marketing campaign for a new coffee brand." 

You can easily search through this list to find specific entries. Just type in a keyword like "work" or "hobby" to quickly filter through your memories. Take your time scrolling through you might be surprised by what you discover, from the very specific to the unexpectedly vague. This is the raw data that shapes your personalized experience.

4. What You'll Likely Find in Your Memory

We're not 100% sure what you might find, but many users have reported seeing details about their interests, professions, and previous topics of discussion. It's a bit fascinating and, honestly, a little eerie to think about how much the AI knows. We'd love to hear your thoughts on this! What have you discovered in your own memory?

5. How to Delete Specific ChatGPT Memories

Once you're in the Manage Memory page, you have full control to delete individual entries:

1. Find the memory item you want to remove by scrolling or searching
2. Click the trash icon next to the specific item
3. Confirm the deletion when prompted

That's it — the memory is gone from ChatGPT's active profile. But here's what most guides don't tell you: deleting individual memories does not remove the underlying conversation data from OpenAI's servers. The memory entries are just derived summaries. The original conversation logs are stored separately and governed by OpenAI's data retention policies (currently up to 30 days for some account types).

To delete a specific memory item fast: Use the search bar on the Manage Memory page with keywords like "job," "location," or "family" to surface and delete clusters of related entries at once rather than hunting through a long list o

By the time you're ready to start your actual work, you might have already spent 45 minutes on these digital chores that a simple automation could handle in seconds. But here's the good news: by 2026, there are free automation tools that have become incredibly user-friendly and effective, making workflow optimization accessible for everyone.

Let's roll up our sleeves and get into the nitty-gritty. Our team is going to walk you through setting up real automations using free versions of Zapier, IFTTT, Microsoft Power Automate, and some fantastic open-source alternatives. Don't worry no coding skills are needed, just a little logical thinking and about 10 minutes of your time.

2. Why Your Brain Is Better Than a Bot

Before we dive in, it's helpful to understand the purpose of automation. It's not about replacing your clever thinking; it's about getting rid of the *tedious tasks*. A study by Asana in 2025 found that knowledge workers spend a whopping 58% of their day on "work about work," like updates and file management, instead of the strategic tasks they were hired to do (Zapier Guides). That's where automation comes in to tackle that 58%!

A good rule of thumb: if you're doing the same task more than three times a week, it's probably a good candidate for automation. Think about it: *IfI receive an email with an invoice attached, *thensave it to my accounting folder. *Ifa new row is added to my spreadsheet, *thencreate a task for me. These predictable, rule-based tasks are exactly what computers are good at!

3. Meet Your Free Toolkit: The Big Three and a Powerful Alternative

You've got four main options here, each with a free tier but differing strengths:

1. Zapier (Free Tier): This is the go-to for connecting apps easily. With the free plan, you can run 100 tasks a month (where each action in a "Zap" counts as a task) and automate every 15 minutes. It connects with over 7,000 apps, making it ideal for cloud-based automations. It's user-friendly, which is perfect if you're just starting out. If you're curious about AI assistants to complement your workflows, check out our ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini guide.

2. IFTTT (If This Then That): This pioneer of simple automations, or "Applets," has a generous free tier, allowing you to create unlimited Applets. It's particularly strong for mobile actions and social media. Think of it as your personal automation toolkit. For instance, "If my Nest Thermostat detects I've left home, then set my office status to 'Working Remotely' in Slack."

3. Microsoft Power Automate (Desktop): A powerful built-in utility for Windows users! The desktop version is free with Windows 10 and 11. While it can connect to cloud services, its superpower is desktop automation literally controlling your mouse and keyboard to automate tasks in applications that don't have modern APIs.

4. n8n (Open-Source Power): If you're a bit tech-savvy and want more control, n8n is an open-source platform that you can run for free on your own computer or a low-cost cloud server. It offers over 350 integrations and allows for complex workflows. While the learning curve is a bit steeper, it gives you unlimited execution and complete privacy.

4. Building Your First Automation: The Automatic Invoice Filer

Let's get practical! Here's a common scenario that many freelancers and office workers encounter: you get an email with a PDF invoice, open it, download the attachment, rename it, and save it to a specific folder. This process takes about 2 minutes each time. Let's see how we can automate this!

Using Zapier (The Easiest Path):
1. Create a New Zap: Head over to zapier.com and sign up for a free account. Click "Create Zap."
2. Set Your Trigger: Search for "Gmail" (or Outlook) and choose the trigger event "New Email with Attachment." Connect your email account and set a specific label or search term to filter the right emails.
3. Test the Trigger: Zapier will pull in a recent email that matches. Pick an actual invoice email for testing.
4. Set Your Action: Search for "Google Drive" and choose the action "Upload File."
5. Configure the Action: For "File," select "1. (New Email with Attachment) File (Exists but not shown)". For "Folder," browse to your "Invoices" folder. For "File Name," use a formula like: .
6. Test and Turn On: Test the action, and if all is good, turn on your Zap. Now every future invoice email that matches your filter will be automatically filed!

## Is ChatGPT Safe in 2026? Enterprise Privacy Audit

**Pillar:** privacy
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/is-chatgpt-safe-2026-security-privacy-guide
**Published:** 2026-06-04

> Is ChatGPT safe for business and personal use? We audited OpenAI data retention policies, zero-data-retention API agreements, SOC 2 compliance, and DLP controls.

As generative AI tools become permanent fixtures on corporate workstations, IT directors and developers face a pressing question: Is ChatGPT safe for production code, sensitive documents, and enterprise data in 2026?

The answer depends heavily on which tier you use, your Data Controls settings, and whether you interact via the web consumer portal or the Platform API.

On our IT workbench, our team conducted a full technical audit of OpenAI’s data retention policies, SOC 2 compliance certifications, API encryption boundaries, and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) guardrails.

Here is our complete enterprise security breakdown, tier comparison matrix, and DLP deployment rules.

🔒 3 Critical Security Risks in ChatGPT (And How to Mitigate Them)

1. Model Training Ingestion (Free & Plus Tiers)
When employees use personal Free accounts, raw prompts can be used by OpenAI to train future public models.
Remediation: If using consumer tiers, navigate to Settings $\rightarrow$ Data Controls and toggle off Improve the model for everyone.

2. Accidental Credential & Token Leaks
Developers frequently paste configuration blocks containing database connection strings, JWT signing keys, or AWS access tokens into chat prompts.
Remediation: Enforce network-level Data Loss Prevention (DLP) proxies to sanitize API keys before transmission.

3. Prompt Injection & Indirect Jailbreaks
When feeding untrusted web content or un-sanitized PDF documents to ChatGPT, malicious prompt injections can trick the model into executing unauthorized tool calls.
Remediation: Restrict autonomous agent tool permissions and sandbox code interpreters in isolated Docker containers.

--
⚡ Implementing Enterprise DLP Regex Rules for AI Traffic

To prevent sensitive tokens and PII from leaving your corporate network to AI endpoints, configure these regex patterns in your Web Gateway / Reverse Proxy:

--
🛡️ Zero Data Retention (ZDR) for OpenAI API

For enterprise applications requiring strict compliance (such as healthcare and legal services), organizations can request Zero Data Retention (ZDR) on the OpenAI Platform API:

1. Under ZDR agreements, prompt payloads and completions are processed strictly in volatile RAM.
2. Data is never written to OpenAI persistent disk storage, even for abuse monitoring.
3. Organizations must maintain their own internal audit logging to satisfy legal discovery requirements.

--
Summary & Further Reading

ChatGPT is safe for enterprise use when operating under ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Team, or the OpenAI Platform API with Data Processing Agreements. However, unmanaged consumer Free accounts pose severe data leakage and IP exposure risks.

## 10 Essential Windows Tweaks to Speed Up a Slow PC (202

**Pillar:** Windows Troubleshooting
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/speed-up-your-slow-pc-in-2026-10-essential-windows-performance-tweaks
**Published:** 2026-06-04

> Your computer used to fly. Now opening a web browser feels like watching paint dry. Speed up your slow PC in 2026 with these 10 tweaks.

1. Speed Up Your Slow PC in 2026: 10 Essential Windows Performance Tweaks

If you've ever felt like your computer is moving at a snail's pace, you're not alone. Remember when your PC zipped along effortlessly? Now, just opening a web browser feels like waiting for paint to dry. With software updates and resource-hungry applications, many of us are in the same boat. In fact, a study from 2025 found that Windows 11 PCs can slow down by about 40% in application launch times after just a year and a half without proper maintenance. (Microsoft PC Manager)

But don't worry! Before you start thinking about buying a new machine, take a deep breath. Most issues are usually due to a buildup of digital clutter and not hardware failures. Just like a bike needs some oil and air in the tires, your PC might just need a few tweaks. Our team has gathered ten practical fixes that you can implement right now no hefty price tag required!

2. Take Control of Your Startup

One of the biggest culprits for slow performance is what's happening right when you start your PC. When you power it on, Windows loads not only the operating system but also a bunch of helper apps and services that you might not even remember installing. These can really slow things down.

To take charge, press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager and click on the "Startup apps" tab. Here, you'll see a list of programs with their "Startup impact" rated as High, Medium, or Low. Right-click any program you don't need at startup like Spotify or printer software and select Disable. This won't uninstall it; it just stops it from launching automatically. You can still open these apps later when you need them. Most people can safely disable over half of these items!

3. Run a Deep Disk Cleanup

Over time, your computer accumulates temporary files and old update leftovers that can take up a lot of space. When your drive is full, Windows struggles to function properly, leading to a slowdown.

To clear this clutter, search for "Disk Cleanup" in the Start menu and run it. Select your C: drive, and after it calculates, click "Clean up system files." Make sure to check all the boxes, especially for "Windows Update Cleanup." You might free up 10-20GB of space! If you want to go further, you could try a tool like BleachBit to target specific application caches.

4. Adjust for Best Performance (or Choose Your Effects)

Windows 10 and 11 have some beautiful visual effects, but they can consume valuable resources. If you want a performance boost, consider turning off most of these effects.

Just type "View advanced system settings" in the Start menu and open it. In the Performance section, click Settings. Here, you can select "Adjust for best performance," which will turn off all visual effects. If you want a balance, you can choose "Custom" and keep the effects you like just be mindful of which ones you choose.

5. Power Plan Optimization

Windows often sets a "Balanced" power plan by default, which can hold back your CPU to save energy. If you're plugged in, let's unleash that power!

Head to Control Panel Hardware and Sound > Power Options. Select "High performance." If you're on a laptop, you'll see options for "Balanced" and "Best performance." You can create a custom plan to ensure your CPU runs at full speed when plugged in.

6. Hunt Down Resource Hogs

Sometimes, a specific program can be the troublemaker. Open Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc) and check the "Processes" tab. Sort by CPU, Memory, and Disk to see what's hogging resources. If you notice an unfamiliar program using a lot of resources, it might be causing issues. You can right-click it and select End task if needed.

7. The Classic Reboot, Done Right

We all know the importance of rebooting, but are we doing it right? Simply clicking "Shut down" may not give you a clean slate. Windows has a feature called Fast Startup that can leave some memory in limbo.

For a fresh start, use "Restart" instead, or hold down the Shift key while clicking "Shut down" for a complete shutdown. Aim to do this at least once a week to clear out any cobwebs.

8. Check for Malware and Adware

Sometimes, performance issues can stem from malicious software lurking in the background. While Windows Security does a decent job, it's a good idea to run a second opinion.

Try a full scan with Windows Security, then consider downloading Malwarebytes Free for an extra layer of protection. It's great at finding unwanted programs that your main antivirus might miss.

9. Reduce Your Browser's Footprint

Often, the slowdown is tied to your web browser. Modern browsers can be resource-intensive, especially with multiple tabs open. 

Start by reviewing your extensions type  (or ) in your address bar. Disable or remove any extensions you don't actively use. You might also want to try tab management extensions like OneTab to save memory.

10. Update Everything (But Do It Wisely)

Keeping your software up to date is crucial for performance. However,

Plus, who hasn't bought a book that quickly becomes outdated? When you hit a snag at 9 PM, it's often too late to ask a colleague for help.

3. Starting from Zero: The Beginner's Workflow

If you're just getting started with Excel, your goal should be to become functional quickly. You want to solve real problems at work or school. Here's how you can use ChatGPT to build your essential skills.

## Technical SEO Checklist for Beginners: 10 Fixes (2026

**Pillar:** Website Setup & SEO
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/technical-seo-checklist-for-beginners-fix-these-issues-to-rank-better
**Published:** 2026-05-26

> You can have the best content on the internet. If your technical SEO is broken, nobody will find it. Fix these 15 issues beginners miss.

1. Technical SEO Checklist for Beginners: Fix These Issues to Rank Better

Have you ever felt like you're shouting into the void? You know your content is great, but if Google can't crawl your site, it's like a brilliant book locked away in a soundproof box. That's where technical SEO comes in it's all about making sure that box is wide open for search engines to explore. Our team has learned that you don't need to be a coding whiz to tackle the most important fixes. Let's walk through some common technical issues that beginners often overlook, and the best part is, most of these can be fixed with just your site settings or user-friendly tools.

2. Your First Tool: Google Search Console

Before diving into fixes, let's arm ourselves with a diagnostic tool. Google Search Console (GSC) is free and super helpful. If you haven't done so yet, make sure to verify your website with GSC. Think of it as your personal hotline to Google. It shows you how Google views your site, any issues it encounters, and which pages are indexed. Start by checking the "Coverage" and "Core Web Vitals" reports in GSC; they'll point out many of the problems we're about to discuss.

3. Site Speed: The Silent Ranking Factor

Did you know that a slow site can affect your ranking? Google loves speed, and users definitely prefer it. A delay of just one second can reduce conversions by 7%! As a beginner, you don't need to stress about achieving a perfect score; instead, focus on finding and fixing the major slowdowns. If your Core Web Vitals aren't up to snuff, check out our Core Web Vitals troubleshooting guide for step-by-step fixes.

Check for slow-loading images. This is often the biggest culprit. Large images can bog down your site, so use free tools like TinyPNG or Squoosh to compress images before uploading. Aim for file sizes under 200KB without sacrificing quality, and remember to size your images appropriately. No need to upload a 4000-pixel image when it will only be displayed at 800 pixels!

Look for excessive redirects. Redirects are when one URL automatically forwards to another. A few are okay, but multiple chains (like Page A -Page B -> Page C) can slow things down. Use a tool like Screaming Frog SEO Spider to identify these chains and update your internal links to point directly to the final destination.

Enable browser caching. This tells your visitors' browsers to save certain files locally, which speeds up their experience when they navigate your site. If you're using a CMS like WordPress, plugins like WP Rocket or even free ones like W3 Total Cache can help set this up with just a few clicks.

4. Mobile-First Indexing: Your Site Must Work on Phones

With Google's mobile-first indexing, it's crucial that your site is mobile-friendly. If it's a headache to navigate on a smartphone, your rankings will suffer, even for desktop searches.

Test your mobile friendliness. Use Google's Mobile-Friendly Test tool to check if your pages are optimized for mobile. It'll highlight any issues, like small text or buttons that are too close together.

Check for intrusive interstitials. These are annoying pop-ups that can cover main content, especially on mobile. Google doesn't like them, so make sure any pop-ups are easy to close and don't obstruct the view right away. A good practice is to show a pop-up after a user has spent some time on the page.

5. Crawl Errors and Broken Links: Opening the Doors for Google

A 404 error is like a dead-end sign for Google crawlers. While a few are normal, a lot of them can indicate a poorly maintained site and can waste your "crawl budget" the limited number of pages Google will crawl at any time.

Review your Crawl Report. Inside Google Search Console, check the "Coverage" report. Look for "Errors" and "Excluded" to see URLs that Google couldn't crawl, often due to 404 or 500 errors. Setting up 301 redirects for moved pages is a common fix here.

Fix internal broken links. Regularly check your website for broken links to other pages. Tools like Screaming Frog or the free Broken Link Checker plugin can help you find these issues. Updating internal links not only enhances user experience but also helps with link equity flow within your site.

6. XML Sitemaps: Giving Google a Map to Your Content

An XML sitemap is like a roadmap for search engines, helping them find your content faster, especially if your site is new or has few links. While it doesn't guarantee indexing, it sure helps!

Find and generate your sitemap. Most modern CMS platforms, like WordPress, create a sitemap automatically. You can usually find it by adding  to your domain. If you don't have one, there are free online generators or plugins to help.

Submit your sitemap to Google Search Console. After locating your sitemap URL, go to the "Sitemaps" section in GSC to submit it. This tells Google where to find your list of pages. Remember to update and resubmit whenever you add or remove significant content.

7. Indexing Issues: Being in
